h1: The 6 Best Small Safes With Keys of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Small Safes With Keys 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 small key-lock safes, from fire-rated SentrySafe boxes to budget steel boxes, compared on fire rating, mounting and keys.
summary: The SentrySafe Fireproof Safe with Key Lock is our top pick, with a UL fire classification and bolt-down hardware. The first SentrySafe chest is a close second, Bonsaii is the best plain steel box, and Yuanshikj is the cheapest.
intro: A key lock never runs out of battery, but its weak point is the key itself. The common mistake is hiding the spare key in the box you cannot open without it.
We reviewed six key-lock safes from the listings and ranked them on fire classification, mounting and keys included. Prices range from under $25 to $100.

products.name: SentrySafe Fireproof Safe with Key Lock, Chest Lock Box for Home or Travel
products.verdict: UL fire classification plus bolt-down hardware.
products.description:
This SentrySafe has a flat key lock, a UL Classified rating of 1/2 hour at 1550 degrees F, bolt-down hardware and a carrying handle, in the $25-50 tier.

It leads because it is the only box here that combines a fire classification with mounting hardware at a low tier. The other SentrySafe chest below it lists no mounting hardware.

It comes with 2 keys. The caveat is that a half hour rating is a baseline, not an extreme level of protection.

products.name: SentrySafe Fireproof Safe Box with Key Lock, Chest Safe with Carrying Handle
products.description:
This SentrySafe chest is UL Classified for 1/2 hour at 1550 degrees F, has a key lock that stops the lid opening during a fire, and carries a lifetime after-fire replacement guarantee.

It ranks second because it lists no mounting hardware and relies on carrying grips. Our data shows no price bucket.

It includes 2 keys. The caveat is that it is easy to carry away.
products.skipIf: You want to bolt it down.

products.name: SentrySafe Black Fireproof and Waterproof Safe, File Folder and Document Box
products.verdict: Hanging file capacity with fire and water protection.
products.description:
This SentrySafe holds hanging file folders, uses a key lock and lists UL Classified fire plus ETL Verified water protection, in the $50-100 tier.

It ranks third because it costs more than the chest safes but adds file capacity and water protection.

It includes 2 keys. The caveat is the higher price tier.

products.name: Bonsaii Security Safe Box with Key Lock, 0.23 Cu.Ft for Cash Jewelry Home
products.verdict: A mountable steel box with hidden hinges.
products.description:
Bonsaii lists 0.23 cu ft, a mountable flat-key design, a pry-resistant door and hidden hinges, in the $25-50 tier.

It ranks fourth because it has no fire rating, unlike the SentrySafe boxes. It also gives guidance on storing the spare key.

It suits cash and jewelry. The caveat is no fire protection.

products.name: Yuanshikj Steel Small Safe Lock Box with Key Security, 0.23 Cu Ft, Black
products.verdict: 2 keys and wall, floor or cabinet mounting.
products.description:
Yuanshikj lists 0.23 cu ft, wall, floor or cabinet mounting or portable use, 2 unique keys and a scratch-resistant coating, in the under $25 tier.

It ranks fifth because it has no fire rating but costs the least.

It suits cash and small items. The caveat is a thin feature list.

products.name: KYODOLED Small Metal Lock Box with Key for Cash and Medication, 2 Keys
products.verdict: A two-layer portable box with a coin tray.
products.description:
KYODOLED is portable with a 2-layer design, a removable 5-compartment coin tray, a carry handle and 2 keys, in the under $25 tier.

It ranks last because it is portable only and not for security against theft.

It suits medication and cash. The caveat is that it cannot be mounted.

methodology.title: Fire classification
methodology.description: UL classified ratings counted heavily, as claims without a classification were treated as unverified.

methodology.title: Extras
methodology.description: Water protection and file capacity counted as extras.

whatMatters.detail: A UL classification means a lab tested the box to a time and temperature, such as 1/2 hour at 1550 degrees F. Marketing claims with no named standard prove nothing. Look for the UL name and numbers in the listing.
A safe you can bolt down resists being carried away. Look for included bolts and pre-drilled holes, not just the word mountable.
A key lock needs a spare, but never inside the box. Look for 2 keys included, and plan a storage spot elsewhere.
Some safes add water protection, usually with an ETL verification. It matters in floods or sprinkler events. Check which standard the listing names.
A deeper box suits cash, a file box suits documents. Check interior dimensions and whether it takes hanging folders.

faq.q: Is a UL fire rating worth it?
faq.a: For documents, yes. It names a tested time and temperature.

faq.q: How do I mount a small safe?
faq.a: Use the included bolts through the pre-drilled holes into a stud or floor.

faq.q: How do I maintain a key lock?
faq.a: Keep keys dry and use the lock occasionally to keep it moving.
The KYODOLED and SentrySafe chests have handles, but they are not theft-proof.

finalTake: The SentrySafe Fireproof Safe with Key Lock is our top pick for fire protection and mounting. Bonsaii is the plain steel choice, and Yuanshikj is the budget buy. Keep your spare key elsewhere.
